Corrected the enumeration and upper-layer quotient. Corrected these and the p_y degree in the Hom base case. The asserted closure of finite sums of shifted words under summands is false: in A2 the longest rank-six summand occurs in the rank-eight sts word. Soergel defines special objects by the stable-sum criterion B+C=D, not by being sums of words. F2 now uses that category and its summand closure; every object of SBim lies in add B and in both flag categories, so Lemma 6.13 yields exactly the unchanged rank sum.

The cited character-recursion item assumes both flags, so it did not justify step 1.4 for a source assumed only in F_Delta. The already declared definition records the separate recursions of Soergel Propositions 5.7 and 5.9. F2 now states and derives each on its proper domain by summing those multiplicities against the normalized Hecke basis, with separate shift rules. Thus left biadjunction induction preserves precisely the stated Delta hypothesis; the dual case and finite sums remain covered without weakening the claim.

D_w is a diagrammatic idempotent object, not yet an identified bimodule, so the least nonzero module-degree argument was unjustified. Its graded endomorphism corner is bounded below because the ambient word Hom has a finite homogeneous R-basis and R is nonnegative. A degree-zero isomorphism to a nonzero shift would give inverse homogeneous units of opposite nonzero degrees; powers of the negative-degree unit contradict that lower bound. This proves shift uniqueness without the later equivalence.

Concatenating arbitrary flags of two summands can violate descending Delta length order: R_e before R_s is the rank-one counterexample. Instead Gamma_A(M prime direct-sum M double-prime) is the direct sum of the two Gamma_A submodules, since support of a pair is the union of its component supports. Consecutive canonical length quotients therefore add, proving multiplicity additivity. F3 also now uses upper Bruhat layers and descending enumeration for Delta, with shift multiplicities determined modulo R_+.

A category having only R and its identity cannot be additive, have shifts, or have End^0(R)=Q. For n=0,1 the repair retains R as the empty word and takes finite sums and shifts with degree-zero bimodule maps and then idempotent completion. Reflection assertions are vacuous in these cases, while the ring, root normalizations and Demazure computations for n>=2 are unchanged.

A permutation is not literally an object of the word category. The cited Construction 6.1 supplies leaves to a chosen reduced expression, and Remark 6.3 requires shared targets. The intended theorem is sound for every such fixed choice, but its notation omitted that choice. Added a common reduced word for each w and typed every leaf to it; the degree of a composite is d(e)+d(f) and the displayed rank now states that sum explicitly.

The original claimed basis values fed three B_s elements to kappa_s:B_s tensor B_s -> B_s, and two B_t elements to mu_t:B_t -> R. Under the correct three-polynomial-slot identification, kappa_s takes the ordered basis u tensor u,u tensor w,w tensor u,w tensor w to 0,0,u/2,w/2. Also mu_t(u_t)=1 and mu_t(w_t)=delta_t. These values give the same -id zig-zag and idempotent decomposition; the example and its verification have been repaired.

The descent argument applied intrinsic multiplicities before establishing flags for arbitrary Karoubi summands. Added the actual word-membership and category dependencies and F6: words have both flags, and the canonical length-layer functors are additive and preserve idempotent summands, so both flag categories are summand-closed (Soergel Remark 5.5 and dual). Step 1.1 now checks membership first. The remaining comparison with the categorification isomorphism and the semilinear bar involution is unchanged.

Step 2.2 already gave the correct two branches, but its later sentence wrongly said the normalized index changes by plus or minus one at every step. The graph-changing branch has unchanged index; only the graph-preserving branch changes it. Corrected this and distinguished the unnormalized generator degree a, which does change by plus or minus one in either branch because length changes by one. The Statement refers to a and remains unchanged, as do the subexpression counts.

ledger_updates.snippet: 1.3 One-colour relations: the dot and trivalent morphisms of one colour are the structure maps of the Frobenius extension $R/R^s$, namely the trace $\partial_s$, the element $\Delta_s$, and the two balanced multiplications; by [F4] the compositions of these maps in $B_s$ satisfy the unit and counit identities of a Frobenius algebra, and the remaining one-colour relation, the vanishing of a circle with a dot, is one of the relations covered by the imported generator check [F7]. It is *not* a consequence of the nonvanishing $\partial_s(\alpha_s)=2\ne0$ alone: that value gives the counit of the unit, and the vanishing of the dotted circle is a separate Frobenius identity, checked on the two generators $1$ and $\alpha_s$ of $R$ over $R^s$. [F2, F3, F4, F7]

use_snippets: [F2] Let $\underline i=(i_1,\ldots,i_r)$ be a word and $B_{\underline i}=B_{i_1}\otimes_R\cdots\otimes_RB_{i_r}$, with $B_\emptyset=R$. Then $B_{\underline i}$ belongs to both $F_\Delta$ and $F_\nabla$, each successive quotient of these flags is a standard bimodule $R_x\{a\}$ with $x$ the product of a subexpression of $\underline i$, and the number of occurrences of a graph $x$ in the $\Delta$-flag and in the $\nabla$-flag of $B_{\underline i}$ is the number of subexpressions of $\underline i$ with product $x$ ([[lem-bott-samelson-bimodules-have-delta-and-nabla-support-filtrations]]).

[F4] $\Delta_x(d)=R_x\{\ell(x)-d\}$ is the standard bimodule $R_x$ with its generator in degree $\ell(x)-d$, where $R_x$ is $R$ with the right action $g\cdot x=gx$ twisted by $x$, and $\operatorname{Hom}_{R\text{-}R}(R_v(a),R_w(b))\cong R(b-a)$ for $v=w$ and $0$ for $v\ne w$; every successive quotient of a $\Delta$-flag is such a standard bimodule, and the layer of length $\ell(x)$ contains the occurrences of the graph $x$ ([[def-type-a-standard-graph-bimodules-support-filtrations-and-character]]).
